key_insight: The paper shows that tensor-network compression can reformulate Fourier-based option pricing so large Carr-Madan computations avoid the memory blowup of explicit FFTs while preserving accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable pathway for financial engineers to price European options on much finer grids using less memory, with a direct bridge to quantum-style Fourier implementations.
method: Recast Carr-Madan option pricing in a tensorized form.
Apply the Superfast Fourier Transform (SFFT), a compressed Tensor Train representation of the QFT.
Compare the classical tensor-network approach with QFT-based simulations and hardware runs.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on European call options report maintained pricing accuracy, substantially reduced memory use, and subexponential scaling versus conventional FFT pricing.
watch_item: Performance depends on tensor compression quality and practical quantum/hardware execution may still face noise and scaling constraints.
paper_title: Classical Tensor Network and Quantum Fourier Transform Approaches for Large-Scale Carr-Madan Option Pricing
